narrative.overview:
The whole product is a mezzotint plate. A mezzotint begins rocked to an even velvet black, and the image exists only where the engraver burnishes the burr back down so it catches light. Movie Passport works the same way: the page, the ocean and every land without films sit in the rocked black, and only what holds cinema (countries with films, the posters standing on them, the thing under the viewer's attention) is burnished up through pewter to silver. Cinema is light pulled out of a dark room; the interface never adds light that does not mean something.

The material is warm, quiet and printed. Panels are the same black lifted a shade and framed by a single hairline, as if printed onto the plate rather than floating above it. Type is engraved: widely tracked roman capitals for names, captions and labels, a screen roman for anything read at length. Corners are square, there is no glass, no blur and no glow; depth comes from offset shadows falling into the black and from brightness, never from translucency. Density is low: the globe stays large at the centre and every overlay keeps to an edge.

The world refuses the category default of a navy space globe with a glowing atmosphere, neon accents and floating rounded poster cards, and refuses the streaming-service look.
keyCharacteristics: Velvet black ground with a fine warm burr of grain over everything.
Silver is the only light; brightness carries meaning (films, selection, attention).
Warm plate brown marks half-scraped states: hover borders, empty selections, dark land.
Engraved Cinzel capitals for names, captions and labels; Spectral for reading.
Square corners, single hairline frames, offset drop shadows, no glass or blur.
Lucide line icons at a 1.5 stroke; one burnished plate button per view.

rules.name: The Silver Means Films Rule
rules.body: On the globe, silver is reserved for countries that have films. A selected country with no films is filled with half-scraped plate and outlined in a silver-bright stroke; it is never filled silver.

rules.name: The One Light Rule
rules.body: There is no accent hue. Emphasis is made by burnishing (velvet, plate, pewter, silver, silver-bright), not by colour. Only film imagery brings colour into the view.

rules.name: The Engraved Capitals Rule
rules.body: Names, captions, labels and actions are set in Cinzel capitals with wide tracking; anything read as a sentence is Spectral. Never set running text in Cinzel, and never set a label in Spectral caps.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: No eyebrow or kicker sits above a heading. An engraved label either is the section heading or sits below a name as its caption (continent and plate code under a country).

rules.name: The Print Spacing Rule
rules.body: Posters on the globe keep about one poster height apart on screen when zoomed in, so no print covers another. Zoomed out, only the best-ranked prints show (12 at the global view, 16 closer, never more than 60), and in film view only about 10 prints stay for context.

rules.name: The Offset Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow is offset downward and falls into the black. No zero-offset glows, no coloured shadows, no glass, no backdrop blur; modal backdrops are plain black at 75%.

rules.name: The Light Follows Attention Rule
rules.body: Posters rest at brightness 0.82 and saturation 0.85, and come to full light on hover, keyboard focus, when pointed at from a list, when selected, or when their country is previewed. In film view every print except the selected or attended one sinks to brightness 0.5. On fine pointers a faint 420px silver radial follows the cursor over the plate. New prints surface out of the dark (from brightness 0.2).

rules.name: The Night Sky Rule
rules.body: The space around the globe is printed in the same mezzotint, never painted as space art: stars are burnished points in silver, warm white and pewter (thicker along the band), and the Milky Way is a mottled haze with dark dust rifts at no more than 30% opacity. It runs as a wandering ring 20 degrees south on the sky, so it passes behind the globe in the opening view however the globe is turned. No blue, no nebula colour, no glow, no twinkle; the sky stays quieter than the land and the posters.
rules.section: The space around the globe is printed in the same mezzotint, never painted as space art: stars are burnished points in silver, warm white and pewter (thicker along the band), and the Milky Way is a mottled haze with dark dust rifts at no more than 30% opacity. It runs as a wandering ring 20 degrees south on the sky, so it passes behind the globe in the opening view however the globe is turned. No blue, no nebula colour, no glow, no twinkle; the sky stays quieter than the land and the posters.

rules.name: The Fleuron Rule
rules.body: The details sheet header is closed by a fleuron rule: two smoke hairlines meeting a small open diamond (a 6px square, rotated 45 degrees, pewter outline). It is drawn, never typed as a glyph.

rules.name: The One Plate Rule
rules.body: A view has at most one burnished plate button: "More details" on the film card, "Play trailer" in the details sheet, "Close" in About, "Try again" on an error. Every other action is a hairline button, a chip or a text link.

rules.name: The Attribution Rule
rules.body: Source credit is part of the design: the TMDB logo and notice in About, a "View on TMDB" link on the film card, JustWatch credited directly under where-to-watch, Natural Earth credited for the map. Credits are set in 13px Spectral pewter with silver underlined links; they are never hidden or removed.

dos: Do let brightness carry meaning: velvet for nothing, plate for half-worked, pewter for half-lit, silver for films and selection, silver-bright for the one live thing.
Do fill a selected empty country with half-scraped plate and outline it in silver-bright.
Do keep one burnished plate button per view and make every other action a hairline button, chip or link.
Do set names, captions and labels in engraved Cinzel capitals with wide tracking, and reading text in Spectral.
Do rest posters at brightness 0.82 and bring them to full light on hover, link, selection or country preview; dim the rest to 0.5 in film view.
Do keep prints about one poster height apart when zoomed in.
Do use lucide icons at strokeWidth 1.5, sized 14px to 16px.
Do keep TMDB and JustWatch attribution visible wherever their data appears.
Do respect reduced motion: panels, prints and the sheet appear without slides.
donts: Don't fill a country silver unless it has films.
Don't round corners on panels, buttons, chips, fields or dialogs; only pins, gauge dots and the loading disc are round.
Don't use glass, backdrop blur, glow or zero-offset shadows; every shadow is offset downward.
Don't introduce an accent hue, neon, or a navy space-globe atmosphere.
Don't place an eyebrow or kicker above a heading.
Don't use Unicode glyphs as icons or ornaments; use lucide for icons and draw rules and fleurons. The middle dot as a text separator is punctuation, not an icon, and stays.
Don't set running text in Cinzel or in capitals.
